title: streaming: lifecycle controls — handle client-cancel, disconnects, reconnect/resume, and server timeouts; OpenAI compat
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improvements to streaming lifecycle: graceful client-cancel handling, robust disconnect/reconnect+resume, server-side timeout tuning for resumed sessions, and OpenAI-streaming compatibility fixes. No user-facing API changes; behavior improves stability for long-lived streams and tool/function-calling flows.
commits: caf3b2a: streaming: add session manager and resumable session tokens
1a9f4d8: streaming handler: observe client-cancel and propagate cancel to runtime
b7e2c5f: openai-compat: map internal close codes to OpenAI stream events
8c4d01a: runtime: ensure function/tool subprocesses terminate on client-cancel
d2f7a30: tests: add integration tests for reconnect/resume and timeout edge cases

description: Context and motivation: We have seen a cluster of incidents where long-running streaming sessions hit partial failures when clients disconnect or cancel while a tool/function call was in progress. Symptoms: orphaned subprocesses for tool calls, dangle in runtime where KV cache offsets diverged, and poor UX when clients attempted to reconnect/resume. This PR implements a coordinated lifecycle model: (1) clear semantics for client-initiated cancel, (2) deterministic handling on client disconnect, (3) resumable sessions using signed resume tokens with offset checkpoints, and (4) server-side timeouts tuned to allow safe reconnect windows. Also includes OpenAI compatibility surface fixes so the behavior matches OpenAI-style stream close events and error codes. Changes in this PR: - session_manager: new component that tracks streaming sessions, issues short-lived resumable tokens, stores last-good token/offset checkpoint per session, and exposes helper APIs to validate resume tokens. - streaming_handler: observes HTTP/WS disconnects and kills or marks sessions for resume depending on disconnect type; on client-cancel explicitly invokes cancellation path that signals runtime and tool subprocesses. - runtime/tool integration: tool/function subprocesses are started under a supervisor; on cancel we send SIGTERM and escalate to SIGKILL after a grace period to avoid orphan processes. - resume protocol: clients receive a resumable token in the final event metadata when the connection is severable; clients can call the same streaming endpoint passing resume_token to continue from the last checkpoint. - server timeouts: default reconnect window increased to 60s for best-effort resume, with configurable bucket for high-throughput flows. - OpenAI compat: adapter maps internal close reasons to OpenAI stream close frames and ensures the last 'done' token is emitted consistently. Backwards compatibility and risk: existing non-resumable flows unchanged. Resume tokens are opt-in and only issued when server detects stream is at a safe checkpoint. Tool-calling semantics: if a client cancels while a tool call is in progress, we will attempt to terminate the tool and emit a structured "tool_cancelled" event to the stream so downstream consumers observe deterministic behavior. Checklist: - [x] new session_manager with unit tests - [x] streaming_handler cancel/disconnect detection - [x] tool subprocess supervisor + termination tests - [x] resume token generation + validation + e2e integration tests - [x] OpenAI compatibility mapping - [x] metrics/tracing for session lifecycle events - [x] docs updated and examples added Tests and CI: added unit tests and integration tests that exercise reconnect/resume and cancel-during-tool scenarios. CI baseline: all checks passed after fixups for flaky test timeouts (see CI comment below). Review conversation (high-level excerpt): - Connor: "Favor explicit resume token expiry + audit log. Also add metrics for 'resume_attempt' and 'resume_success'." - Author (Aisha): "Added expiry (default 60s) and two counters: streaming_resume_attempts, streaming_resume_success_total; included in observability docs." - Miguel: "How do we guarantee function outputs are not duplicated on resume?" - Author: "We checkpoint function call completion markers in the session checkpoint; resume only allowed at safe checkpoints. If resume happens mid-tool-call we return a 409/resume-not-available and instruct client to retry non-resumable route." - Zoe: "Edge cases: connection flaps and double-reconnect race." - Author: "Added optimistic locking on session record and unit tests to validate the race." CI notes: initial run showed flakes in tests/integration/test_reconnect_resume.py due to timeouts; increased waits and added retry logic in test harness. Final CI run: all checks green (unit, integration, lint, mypy, fmt). Merge notes: squash-and-merged after approvals from reviewers. Post-merge tasks: monitor streaming_resume_success_total and streaming_resume_failure_total for first 48h. Operational runbook updated in docs/streaming.md. Additional context: a short-term hotfix branch was cut in SUP-881 to address a production incident; this PR consolidates the hotfix with the longer-term resume implementation.
